ages: Military obligation of men by law — up to about age 45 (exact limits not confirmed in the sources found; Wikipedia mentions "all men up to 45" for the exit rule)
naturalized: Naturalized citizens have the same obligations as other Germans (no separate exceptions found in the sources). Since 1 January 2026 the military service modernization law applies: all 18-year-old men must fill in a questionnaire, a mandatory medical examination (Musterung) — starting with men born in 2008. Conscription itself is not yet mandatory; the «Bedarfswehrpflicht» (including selection by lot) is introduced only by a separate Bundestag law if volunteer recruitment is insufficient.
abroad: By law men under 45 need Bundeswehr permission to leave Germany for longer than 3 months, but Minister Pistorius suspended this requirement by a directive of 7 April 2026 (the provision of the law remains).
buyout: There is no paid buy-out. Conscientious objection (Kriegsdienstverweigerung) is guaranteed by the Basic Law; details of alternative service in the event of a possible Bedarfswehrpflicht were not found in the sources.
